description: A one-shot mono bass voice: a trigger fires a note with a decay envelope, two fixed timbres and a single bipolar filter macro.

params.text: Fires a note each time it is pressed.
One knob for both filters: at the centre neither is in circuit, left brings in a low-pass from 20kHz down to 20Hz, right a high-pass from 20Hz up to 20kHz, with resonance rising at each end.
Sets the decay time of the envelope, from 80ms at the far left to 800ms at the far right on an exponential scale.
Chooses timbre 1, a near-sine with a gentle drive, or timbre 2, a square and saw blend with a 45Hz high-pass in front, a sub an octave down, a tanh shaper and a 6kHz low-pass after.

inputs.text: A rising edge past 1V fires a note; the edge is armed again below 0.1V.
Sets the pitch at 1V per octave around the base note, clamped to ±2 octaves; with nothing patched the voice plays about 65.4Hz.
Adds to the FILTER knob one for one over the same -10 to +10 span.
Adds to the DECAY knob one for one over the same -10 to +10 span, and is read at the moment a note fires.

notes: Pulling the cable out of V/OCT fires a note by itself and returns the voice to its base pitch.
A trigger does not reset the oscillator phase, so repeated notes start from wherever the waveform had reached.
An anti-click ramp of about half a millisecond is applied at the start of every note, ahead of the envelope.

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
1V per octave · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads the base note, about 65.4Hz.
inputs.2:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±10V.
inputs.3:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±10V.
